quiet: The Hansa's old hall at Alpha has a museum wing now. Its queue is shorter than the hiring hall's.
Alpha's ring traffic never stops. The controllers sleep in shifts, and so do the ships.
Beta's farm drums turn overhead, slow as a held breath. Somewhere up there a trading house is burning a surplus.
The cargo ring smells of wet soil from the drums. Even the steel here is a little green.
Lift cages rattle up from the deep levels with a shift's worth of tired faces. Nobody looks at the button for level nine.
Gamma's company store still prints its prices on paper, so nobody can say they changed overnight.
A hovertank skims the test strip past the plant, its skirt hissing on the dust. Then another. Then the first one back.
Geod's Row runs green to the horizon. The land next to it is fenced, and the fence is very well kept.
Epsilon's promenade still flies the banners of a gala nobody remembers. The holograms on them have faded to ghosts of ghosts.
The needle office at Epsilon posts its timetable in three calendars: dock time, ship time and 'other'.

Ancient Ruins Alpha.system: Tau Ceti, in the debris disk

Ancient Ruins Beta.system: Epsilon Indi, a moon of the cold giant Ab

vault_word.title: the word that opens the Kraal vault
vault_word.about: In 2533 {neon_sleeper} has slept too long in stasis and lost the word she chose for the family vault in 2460; the chambers take the newest memories first. In Cargo 2, newly awake at Delta, she chooses it and tells the captain. Back in 2533, the word opens the vault.

vertex_array.about: In 2533 {ancient_scholar}'s notes have a gap where the shape of the missing segment should be: measured from the samples, lost in the Institute fire. In Cargo 1 the captain measures the three samples at the Stellar Institute before the fire and gives her the cartridge, labelled in the captain's hand. Back in 2533 the cartridge is in her notes: the Vertex Array, which the restart will need.

intro.again.text: {origin.name} has been through 2533 once already, as {origin.rank}. The hiring hall at {place} has your face on file under another date. The clerk decides it is a filing error. In a way, it is.

intro.from_cargo2.text: {origin.name} flew the needles of 2460 as {origin.rank}. That was seventy-three years ago by the dock clocks, and a good deal less by yours. The ring you chased is a joke now. The Debacle made it one.

intro.colonel.text: {origin.name} took {serac}'s commission a hundred and thirteen years ago. The Mandate kept your rank warm. The pension office keeps it under 'missing, presumed timeless'.

intro.founder.text: {origin.name} was one of the captains who founded the Hauler Hansa. The Hansa is a hundred and thirteen years old now, and has a museum. You are in it, in a glass case marked 'presumed'.

intro.from_cargo1.text: {origin.name}, {origin.rank}, flew when the Hansa was new. That was a hundred and thirteen years ago by the dock clocks. Long sublight legs and longer sleeps kept you younger than the calendar. The calendar has not forgiven you.

intro.fresh.text: 2533. You have a captain's licence and a kit bag. The licence says captain. The hiring hall at {place} says able hand, and the hall is the one that is hiring.

opening.pod.title: The needle
text: Your first command went into the needle at Beta with a full hold. The needle shed you like a bad link: one moment the file of ships, the next a pod tumbling in the dark.

The pod kept you cold and asleep for nineteen years, until a salvager found it. The salvager claimed the pod and paid you a finder's tenth of your own scrap value: three hundred credits. Your ship did not come with you.
The needle shed you again. You know the drill by now: the file of ships, the jolt, the pod tumbling in the dark, and the long cold sleep.
The salvager who found you this time paid a finder's tenth of your own scrap value, three hundred credits, and asked if you did this on purpose. Your ship did not come with you. It never does.

hall.first.title: The hiring hall
text: The hiring hall at {place} is a long room with a berths board at one end and the plants' shift lists at the other. Captains post what they want and what they pay. Nobody posts what they carry.

The old hands on the benches talk about people who should be dead. A loader agrobot one hand short, older than the Hansa, still works the cargo rings. A singer rides every needle and never gets older. And a man called {serac} has not aged a day since the Debacle, or since long before it.

thought.first_work.text: No ship. The berths board pays on arrival, the plants pay by the shift, and either way I learn something.

thought.find_adit.text: The old hands say the loader agrobot works the cargo rings, Beta most of all, two turns at a dock and then on. If anything on the docks remembers my century, it does. It likes people who work the ring.

thought.the_pod.text: The world moved on while I slept in the pod. First find out who is still in it, then what became of my ship.

thought.never_came_out.text: My ship never came out of the needle. Somebody who rides the needles might know where they really go.

floor.hovertank.title: The hovertank plant
floor.hovertank.text: The plant builds hovertanks for whoever pays, the Mandate this year. The foreman says the design goes back to a legion prototype that came to Delta a century ago, flipped once, and was never quite the same.

variants.text: The first drawing in the plant's lobby is the legion's prototype, the one you delivered to Delta c a century ago. Someone has written 'mind the skirt' in the margin. The line still builds it, for the Mandate this year.
The plant's licence came through {serac}'s depot a century ago, with the prototype you sold him. The foreman calls the design 'the colonel's tank' and does not know which colonel.

floor.mine.title: The deep levels
floor.mine.text: The deep levels go down eleven now. The old hands will not go below nine, and nobody says why.

variants.text: On level nine there is a plaque with twelve names, and a thirteenth: yours. The old hands touch it for luck and will not go below nine. Now you know why they stop there.
On level nine there is a plaque with twelve names, and a thirteenth line you let stay blank. The old hands touch it for luck and will not go below nine. Now you know why they stop there.
On level nine there is a plaque with twelve names, and a thirteenth line left blank 'for the hauler'. The old hands will not go below nine. Now you know why they stop there.
Far down the galleries a mining agrobot with a Rockwarden share badge is still boring the first gallery's fourth extension. {aela} does not stop to look. It never did. Next time, perhaps.

floor.biomass.title: The farm drums
floor.biomass.text: The farm drums turn all shift. The agrobots tend the crops, the people tend the agrobots, and nobody tends the people.

variants.text: When you clock in, the agrobots pass a pulse of light down the row. The Sowers kept the relay you let them keep, and it is a node now. Nodes remember.
Geod's Row grows from the seed stock you brought a century ago. The tender beside you says the first fields were 'given by a hauler', as if haulers gave things.

hands.plumb.title: {plumb}
hands.plumb.text: {plumb} checks her own manifest twice, then yours. 'I pay what the board says,' she says. 'The board says less than the others. That is how you know it is true.'

hands.ghillie.title: {ghillie}
hands.ghillie.text: {ghillie} named his ship the Low Water, he says, because that is when you find what people dropped. He does not say what he carries. He pays half again, and he does not ask what you carried either.

hands.caspic.title: {caspic}
hands.caspic.text: {caspic} has orders for everything, including you. 'Navigator, gunner or steward. The Mandate does not hire loaders. Loaders ask about crates.'

variants.text: {caspic} reads your file and salutes. Then he reads the date on it and stops saluting. 'Navigator, gunner or steward,' he says. 'Sir. Or not, sir. I will ask.'

hands.vrtoch.title: {vrtoch}
hands.vrtoch.text: The Errata is the last ring-research ship nobody impounded, because nobody could find its registration. 'We measure the Gyrotron's silence,' says {vrtoch}. 'It is a very precise silence.'

hands.caboose.title: {caboose}
hands.caboose.text: {caboose} blesses your kit bag 'in apparent good order and condition'. His papers say {caboose.full}, from his scan code; the old hands still call him Officer Deks, from before the Cargolytes relabelled him. The Clean Lading rides at the tail of every needle, where the Sender looks first. It is cold back there, the pay is low, and nobody asks your name.

friends.adit.title: {dock_loader}
text: The old loader agrobot works beside you for a whole shift without a word. At the end it corrects your grip. 'You will last,' it says. From {dock_loader.short}, that is a speech.
'I keep lists,' it says. 'Every hull that went into the yards after the Debacle, and every name on every tag. Ask.'
{dock_loader} still has the hand you brought back from Geod's Row, and the hand still says USE NO HOOKS. It knows you before you speak. 'Seventy-three years,' it says. 'I kept it oiled.'
'I keep lists now,' it says. 'Every hull that went into the yards after the Debacle, and every name on every tag. Ask.'
{dock_loader} turns its sensor head when you pass. 'Beta, 2460,' it says. 'You stacked badly then too.'
'I keep lists now. Every hull that went into the yards after the Debacle, and every name on every tag. Ask.'
'The old manifests have your name,' says {dock_loader}. 'Your crates were always square. The loaders talked about you, the ones who trained me.'
'I keep lists. Every hull that went into the yards after the Debacle, and every name on every tag. Ask.'

friends.adit_ship.text: {dock_loader} runs its lists, twice. 'Every hull that came out of a needle since the Debacle is in here,' it says. 'Yours went in. It never came out. Neither did the file it flew with.' It thinks about that. 'Ask {warp_singer}. She rides every needle. She would know where they go when they do not come back.'

Neither did the file it flew with.' It thinks about that. 'You speak needle-talk. So does {warp_singer}. Ask her what the needle said to you.'

friends.adit_who.text: '{aela} still digs for the Rockwardens,' says {dock_loader}. '{neon_sleeper} sleeps at Delta between decades. {warp_singer} rides every needle and does not age. {serac} does not age either, but nobody calls him a friend. He asked about you last month.'

friends.adit_work.text: You work the next shift beside {dock_loader}. It never says a word you did not need, and by the end your grip is right. 'Now ask me something,' it says. 'Friends ask.'

sight.gamma.plaque.title: Level nine's plaque
text: Down on level nine, by the lift, hangs a plaque from 2420, cut with a borrowed laser: the twelve miners who came out, and under them a thirteenth line, blank, 'for the hauler who brought the air'.
Nobody alive knows who that was. The miners touch the blank line for luck on the way down.
Down on level nine, by the lift, hangs a plaque from 2420, cut with a borrowed laser: the twelve miners who came out, and a thirteenth line for the hauler who brought the air. It says {player_name}.
The letters are worn smooth where a century of miners touched them for luck. A boy in a lift cage reads your name off the plaque, then off your tag, and decides it is a coincidence.

Down on level nine, by the lift, hangs a plaque from 2420, cut with a borrowed laser: the twelve miners who came out, and a thirteenth line, still blank. A man with a borrowed laser once asked you for a name, and you let it stay blank.
'Blank is honest,' he said. The miners touch it for luck on the way down, and wonder.

Down on level nine, by the lift, hangs a plaque from 2420, cut with a borrowed laser: the twelve miners who came out, and a thirteenth line, blank, 'for the hauler who brought the air'. You have promised it a name.
2420 is a needle and a Gyrotron turn away. Your record carries the errand.
Down on level nine, by the lift, hangs a plaque from 2420, cut with a borrowed laser: the twelve miners who came out, and a thirteenth line, blank, 'for the hauler who brought the air'.
That was you, in 2420. You left Gamma before the plaque was cut, and nobody wrote the name down.

thought.errand.plaque.text: Level nine's thirteenth line waits for a name. The way back to 2420 is my record: export it with 'captain', start Cargo 1 as this captain, and get the miners out of level nine at Gamma.

sight.delta.conte.title: {neon_sleeper}
text: {neon_sleeper} is awake for the restart, barely older than in 2460. She sits on the steps of the Kraal counting room with a cup of coffee, in front of a vault that will not open.

'I chose the word myself,' she says. 'Seventy-three years in the chamber, and it went first. The chambers take the newest memories first.' The vault holds what the family kept back from the Debacle. She will share it with whoever brings the word back.

text: Errands to the past travel in your captain's record. To take this one to 2460, use 'captain' to export your record, then start Cargo 2 (2.3.0 or newer) as this captain.

In 2460, {neon_sleeper.short} still sleeps at Delta and wakes on her own schedule. Be there when she does, and be in the room when she chooses the word. Then start Cargo 3 again as this captain: in that 2533 you will know it.

thought.errand.vault.text: {neon_sleeper.short} lost the word for her vault in the chamber. The way back to 2460 is my record: export it with 'captain', start Cargo 2 as this captain, and be at Delta when she first wakes.

thought.vault_word.text: I know the word for the Kraal vault. I was there when it was chosen. {neon_sleeper.short} sits at Delta in front of a door she cannot open.

errand.vault.opened.text: The vault opens with a sigh of old air. Between deeds to land nobody has seen in a century lies a grey instrument the size of a hand: a Procrustes Analyzer. It turns two shapes until they match, whatever angle each is seen from. 'My father bought it to find ships that changed their names,' {neon_sleeper.short} says. 'Take it. You have one to find.'

sight.epsilon.notes.title: {ancient_scholar}'s notes
text: The Concord keeps a reading room at Epsilon that nobody reads in. One shelf holds {ancient_scholar}'s notes: forty years in her hand, then decades more from her upload, which writes neater than she did.
One page has a gap where the shape of the missing segment should be. 'Measured from the samples, Stellar Institute, 2420,' it says. 'Lost in the fire.'

sight.alpha.yard.title: The impound yard
text: Behind a fence at the edge of Alpha's ring, the Mandate keeps the hulls that touched the Gyrotron before the Debacle. They wait for an audit nobody will hold.
The {perimeter_guard} walks the fence with a rifle slung the comfortable way, and does not look at you twice.

variants.text: The impound yard. The {perimeter_guard} nods to you now, the way you nod to a debt.

yard.ask.text: 'Nothing in there came out of a needle,' the {perimeter_guard} says. 'Ask the docks. There is a loader one hand short that keeps lists. It knows more than the Mandate does, and the Mandate does not like that.'

variants.text: 'Nothing in there came out of a needle,' the {perimeter_guard} says. 'You know {dock_loader}? Then you know more than I do. Everyone does. I just walk the fence.'

text: Forty-one hulls, each with a registry and an audit date that came and went. And one with neither: towed in last year, tumbling, from no needle anybody logged. The paint is new. The hull under it is not.
'Not yours?' the {perimeter_guard} asks. 'Didn't think so. Nobody's is.'

Forty-one hulls, each with a registry and an audit date that came and went. And one with neither: towed in last year, tumbling, from no needle anybody logged. The paint is new. The hull under it is not.
The Procrustes Analyzer turns the nameless hull over and over and gives up: it has been cut and welded too often to match anything. Somebody did not want it found.

people.medic.title: {medic}
people.medic.text: A {medic} has a folding table at the end of the berths, a case of patches and a hand-painted sign: CASH, NO NAMES.

variants.text: The {medic} at the end of the berths looks at the way you stand and pushes a stool at you before you ask. The sign says CASH, NO NAMES.

text: '{caboose} sends me his crews with notes pinned to their shirts,' the {medic} says. '{caspic} sends nobody, and his crews come anyway. {ghillie}'s people pay double and lie about how they got hurt.'
She does not say who pays her. She taps the sign.

sight.epsilon.clinic.title: A clinic off the research ring
sight.epsilon.clinic.text: Off Epsilon's research ring there is a clinic with one chair, and the chair has seen better centuries. The {cybersurgeon} fits implants for hands who need to be better than they are, and reads old damage for those who want to know. Her prices climb with every level, and with every implant already in you.

choices.say: Have the pod's damage read (20 credits)
Look at the implant catalogue (a level of a skill; dear, and dearer)
Keep your head as it is

clinic.scan.text: The {cybersurgeon} reads the scan the way a pilot reads weather. 'The cold took the newest memories first. That is what cold does. The last weeks before the needle are gone, and they are not coming back. Not from me.'

text: The {cybersurgeon} reads the scan the way a pilot reads weather. 'The cold took the newest memories first. That is what cold does.'
'{neon_sleeper.short} sat in this chair last month. She wanted a word back. I told her what I am telling you: the cold keeps nothing. If you want something back, ask the past.'

sight.delta.range.title: The test range
sight.delta.range.text: Out on the test range a hovertank idles on its skirt. The {battle_engineer} is under it with a torch. The {armored_commander} sits in the hatch with a slate and a cold coffee, and watches the dust.

variants.text: {gabion} is under the hovertank again. She waves the torch at you, which on the range counts as a greeting. The {armored_commander} raises the cold coffee.

text: Out on the test range a hovertank idles on its skirt. The {battle_engineer} is under it with a torch. The {armored_commander} sits in the hatch with a slate and a cold coffee, and watches the dust.
The {battle_engineer} does not look up from the skirt. Somebody behind you says 'line crosser' to nobody in particular.
Out on the test range a hovertank idles on its skirt. The {battle_engineer} is under it with a torch. The {armored_commander} sits in the hatch with a slate and a cold coffee, and watches the dust.

'The first of these came to Delta c in a hauler's hold, a century and more ago,' the {battle_engineer} says from under the skirt. 'We still build to its drawings. The delivery note is signed, and nobody can read the name.'
Out on the test range a hovertank idles on its skirt. The {battle_engineer} is under it with a torch. The {armored_commander} sits in the hatch with a slate and a cold coffee, and watches the dust.
'The licence came through {serac}'s depot,' the {armored_commander} says. 'Everything good comes through his depot in the end. That is what worries me.'

choices.say: Ride as gunner in a live-fire trial (gunner: able or better)

range.rig.text: You hold the skirt panels while the {battle_engineer} welds them. She works fast and says nothing until the last seam. 'You have done this before,' she says. 'Not on a tank. On something that mattered more to you.'

range.ride.text: The {armored_commander} keeps the tank at a crawl and the targets honest. You hit four of six. 'You shoot like somebody who learned on a hauler,' the {armored_commander} says. '{serac}'s people shoot like that too. For other reasons.'

range.named.text: 'Gabion,' she says, without looking up. 'A wire cage full of rock. I build walls overnight, and the crew stopped using my rank the week I stopped a tank with one.' She holds out a hand with a burn across the palm. 'Now you know. Don't spread it around.'

squad.sweep.title: A sweep
text: A {infantry_squad} works down the berths, checking papers. Their {heavy_infantry_commander} reads names off a slate and does not look up until yours.
'{player_name}. Pod survivor.' A pause. 'You are on a list, hand. Not ours.' He puts the slate away. '{serac} likes to find people himself.'
A {infantry_squad} works down the berths, checking papers. Their {heavy_infantry_commander} reads names off a slate and does not look up until yours.
'{player_name}. Inner-systems wing, a commission nobody closed.' He looks at you properly for the first time. 'You are on {serac}'s list, not ours. He likes to find people himself.'
A {infantry_squad} works down the berths, checking papers. Their {heavy_infantry_commander} reads names off a slate and does not look up until yours.
'{player_name}.' A pause. 'You are on a list, hand. Not ours. {serac}'s own, in his own hand, which is never good news.'

choices.say: Carry the commander's kit to the next berth (loader practice)
Slip away through the cargo ring (navigator: green or better)

squad.carry.text: The kit weighs as much as you do. The {infantry_squad} relaxes a little, the way soldiers do around anyone who carries something for them. The {heavy_infantry_commander} says nothing more about lists, which is a kind of thanks.

squad.slip.text: You know the cargo ring better than the squad does. By the time the {heavy_infantry_commander} looks up again you are three berths away and somebody else's problem. He will remember the face.

sight.beta.needle_office.title: The needle office
text: Beta's needle office: one window, one {needle_clerk}, and a board of what is on at every dock, chalked fresh each turn.
The board says: {labour_news}
Beta's needle office has a customs desk inside it this week, and the {needle_clerk} stamps every manifest twice.
The board says: {labour_news}

choices.say: Ask about the needle that shed you

clerk.needle.text: 'Your needle filed one hull more at the buoy than it filed at the far end,' the {needle_clerk} says, without looking it up. 'It happens. Not often. Ask {warp_singer}: she rides every needle and remembers every one. I only stamp them.'

sight.gamma.store.title: The company store
sight.gamma.store.text: Gamma's company store sells a miner everything at a price only a miner would pay. The {store_cashier} takes scrip, cash and notice, in that order.

variants.text: The shafts are shut for gas, and the company store is full of miners who cannot earn. The {store_cashier} writes credit she knows will never come back.

Gamma's company store sells a miner everything at a price only a miner would pay. The {store_cashier} looks at you and rounds your bill down. 'You went down with the fire boss,' she says. 'Word gets round.'

choices.say: Ask who pays cash at Gamma

store.tab.text: The tab belongs to a shaft sinker with two children and one boot. She does not thank you; miners don't. Word of it goes round the deep levels the way gas does.

store.cash.text: '{aela},' the {store_cashier} says. 'An agrobot that still digs for the Rockwardens and pays its crew in cash. The company hates it. It asks every new hand whether they are in the cooperative.'

text: '{aela},' the {store_cashier} says. 'An agrobot that still digs for the Rockwardens and pays its crew in cash. The company hates it.'
'It asked after you once. It said you gave it a share, a hundred years ago, and that a share is forever.'

people.auditor.title: {hansa_auditor}
people.auditor.text: A {hansa_auditor} has the ring's manifests spread over three tables, with a fourth on order. The smugglers have found somewhere else to be.

choices.say: Help with the count (broker practice, 50 credits)
Leave the auditor to the count

auditor.count.text: You count crates until the numbers stop meaning anything. '{plumb},' the {hansa_auditor} says at the end, closing a ledger. 'The only manifest on this ring I have never had to count twice. Honest as a plumb line, and about as much fun.'

people.tail_gunner.title: {tail_gunner}
people.tail_gunner.text: The convoy's {tail_gunner} is drinking at the end of the ring, because tail gunners always end up at the end of things.

choices.say: Buy a drink and ask about the back of a convoy (10 credits)
Leave the gunner to the drink

tailgun.talk.text: 'Raiders hit the third hull in a file, never the last,' the {tail_gunner} says. 'The last is us, or it is {caboose}'s lot, singing. Nobody wants to board a ship full of people singing.'

people.prospector.title: {rockwarden_prospector}
people.prospector.text: A {rockwarden_prospector} in a cooperative jacket is buying claims on the new seam before the company can file them.

choices.say: Sell her your survey of the seam (navigator: able or better)

prospector.survey.text: She pays in cash, counts it twice, and writes your name in a book with a stone on the cover. 'The cooperative remembers who helped,' she says. 'Stonewright's people are coming home. They will want to know.'

prospector.coop.text: '{aela} dug our first gallery, a hundred years before I was born,' the {rockwarden_prospector} says. 'It still asks everyone whether they are in the cooperative. Most of us say yes, to be kind. Some of us mean it.'

people.squad.title: {infantry_squad}
people.squad.text: The {infantry_squad} is back on the berths. The {heavy_infantry_commander} nods to you, which is worse than not nodding.

variants.text: The {infantry_squad} is back on the berths. The {heavy_infantry_commander} nods to you like a colleague. That is worse.
The {infantry_squad} is back on the berths. The {heavy_infantry_commander} does not nod. He writes something on the slate instead.

thought.ship_needs.text: A ship needs more than a hull: someone to vouch for me, papers, a debt I can call in, a navigator's key for the needles, and the truth about the ship I lost. Three of those, and I could start looking for one.

thought.korai.text: {warp_singer} rides every needle: Beta, Epsilon, Beta, Delta. She could teach me the count that tells a needle where to put a ship, if I can hold a count: a green navigator, at least.

thought.eela.text: {aela} still digs in Gamma's deep levels. The Rockwarden cooperative vouches for its own, and {aela} decides who its own are.

thought.papers.text: A ship needs papers. The Kraal family charters captains, and its counting room is at Delta.

thought.seal.text: The Kraal seal is in a yacht in the Mandate's impound yard at Alpha. The guard takes money; the fence is low.

thought.seal_held.text: I have the Kraal seal. The Pfennig at Delta can write my papers with it.

thought.voce.text: {meza_voce} runs food from Beta's farm drums to Gamma's miners, two turns at each. The Rootstock pay their debts, both kinds.

thought.voce_run.text: {meza_voce}'s crates go to the gallery gate at Gamma, past the company's guards.

thought.cu113.text: There is a hull with no name in the Mandate's impound yard at Alpha, and a machine inside the fence that counts the hulls.

friends.korai.title: {warp_singer}
text: {warp_singer} sits in the needle office's signal loft with her boots on the rail, humming at the buoy. She looks twenty-five. She was twenty-five in 2460.

'Needles don't lose ships,' she says. 'They put them where the file says. Yours flew without a file, so the needle put it where it liked.' There is a count, she says, that tells a needle where to put you. She will teach it to someone who can hold it through a jump.

variants.text: {warp_singer} is in the signal loft again, humming. 'Can you hold a count yet?' she asks.

text: {warp_singer} sits in the needle office's signal loft, humming at the buoy, and stops halfway through a bar. 'You still have the verse,' she says. 'I can hear it in how you stand.'

'Needles don't lose ships. They put them where the file says. Yours flew without a file.' The verse you learned in 2460 is half of the count that tells a needle where to put you. She can teach you the other half.
{warp_singer} sits in the needle office's signal loft, humming at the buoy. 'Beta, 2460,' she says, without turning round. 'You asked me where the needles go. I said ask me later. It's later.'

'They don't lose ships. They put them where the file says. Yours flew without one.' There is a count that tells a needle where to put you, and she will teach it to someone who can hold it through a jump.

choices.say: Sing her the verse she taught you
Ride the next needle with her and hold the count (navigator: green or better)
Ask her how the count goes

friends.korai_learn.text: She counts it for you, slowly, tapping it on the rail: eleven beats and a held one, then nine. You lose it at the held one. 'Everyone does,' she says. 'Come back when you can hold a count through a jump. Sign on as a navigator somewhere. The needles teach it if you let them.'

text: You ride the file of the next needle in the signal pod at its head, with {warp_singer} beside you and forty haulers behind. When the needle takes hold, the stars go long and she starts to sing.
Eleven beats and a held one, then nine. The held beat is where the needle listens. Halfway through, the file shudders, and the count wants to go with it.

choices.say: Hold the count, and ask her where the needle put your ship

friends.korai_key.text: 'That's the key,' {warp_singer} says, when the stars come back. 'Not a thing. A count. A navigator who holds it can ask a needle to put a ship where they want it, and sometimes when.' She writes the numbers on the back of your hand, in case. You will not need them.

friends.korai_yard.text: 'Late,' she says. 'A ship without a file comes out late. Years, sometimes a century. Look for a hull that came out of no needle anybody logged. The Mandate tows those to Alpha and paints over them.'

friends.eela.title: {aela}
text: A mining agrobot the size of a shuttle works the face on level nine, with a cooperative badge welded to its cab. It stops when you come near. 'Are you in the cooperative?' it asks. It asks everyone.
{aela} has found a seam of its own, and claim jumpers come down for it every night shift. 'The cooperative vouches for its own,' it says. 'I decide who its own are. Mostly I decide yes.'

variants.text: {aela} is back at its seam. The claim jumpers came again last night. 'Are you in the cooperative yet?' it asks. 'I am still deciding.'

text: {aela} stops digging when you come near, and turns its whole cab to look at you. 'You put me in the cooperative,' it says. 'The first machine shareholder. A hundred and thirteen years of dividends, and nothing to spend them on.'
It has found a seam of its own, and claim jumpers come down for it every night shift. 'The cooperative vouches for its own,' it says. 'You are its own. I checked the book.'

choices.say: Ask it to vouch for you
Survey the seam for the cooperative (navigator: able or better)
Stand on its seam with it when the claim jumpers come
Tell it you are still deciding too

friends.eela_held.text: The claim jumpers go back up the shaft without the seam. {aela} watches them go, then writes in the cooperative's book with one careful manipulator: your name, and after it, 'decided'. 'Now you are in the cooperative,' it says. 'Anyone who asks, the cooperative vouches for you.'

friends.eela_lost.text: The claim jumpers take the night's ore. {aela} digs on. 'They will come back,' it says. 'So can you.'

friends.eela_vouch.text: A prospector in a cooperative jacket comes down with the book, and {aela} watches your name go into it. 'Anyone who asks,' the prospector says, 'the cooperative vouches for you. Some people will ask. Some of them are family.'

friends.conte_papers.title: The Kraal counting room
text: Inside the Kraal counting room, {heritarchist.short} keeps the family's charter book: a Pfennig, though nobody is sure which one, and he does not say.

'The family charters captains,' he says. 'Papers that any needle office honours, and some that ask no questions. A charter needs the family seal. The seal is in a yacht the Mandate impounded after the Debacle, in its yard at Alpha. The Mandate will release the yacht after an audit, which it will not hold.'

variants.text: When you hold up the seal, {heritarchist.short} looks at it, then at you, and opens the charter book without a word.

text: Inside the Kraal counting room, {heritarchist.short} keeps the family's charter book. 'My grandfather read your family line,' he says, 'and billed the Conte for it. We still have the bill.' Or perhaps it was him; with Pfennigs, nobody is sure.
'The family charters captains. A charter needs the family seal, and the seal is in a yacht the Mandate impounded after the Debacle, in its yard at Alpha.'

choices.say: Say you will fetch the seal
Pay for papers the long way: 2,500 credits and a stack of forms

friends.seal_asked.text: He writes you a letter on the family's paper: the bearer acts for the Kraal family in the matter of a yacht. 'The guard at the yard cannot read,' he says, 'but he can count. And the fence is lower than the Mandate thinks.'

friends.yard_seal.title: The Kraal yacht in the yard
friends.yard_seal.text: The Kraal yacht sits at the end of a row of impounded hulls, gold leaf peeling off its nose. The seal will be in the owner's cabin. The {perimeter_guard} walks the fence, and the night watch comes on at the change of shift.

choices.say: Pay the guard 300 credits to look the other way
Show the guard the Pfennig's letter (broker: able or better)
Go over the fence at night

friends.seal_taken.text: The owner's cabin smells of a century of closed air. The seal is in the desk, on a chain, heavier than it looks: a crest of a cattle pen, which is what Kraal means.

friends.seal_night.text: You come back over the fence with the seal on its chain round your neck and the night watch behind you. They do not follow you past the fence. The Mandate does not pay them for that.

friends.seal_lost.text: The night watch takes the seal off you and puts it back in the yacht, carefully. The Mandate keeps a list of what is in every hull. It does not keep a list of who tried.

friends.conte_signed.text: Back at Delta, {heritarchist.short} presses the seal into the charter book, and {neon_sleeper} signs it on her way past with a coffee in the other hand. 'A family captain,' she says. 'Try not to embarrass us. We have been embarrassed by experts.' Your papers say you may command a ship under the Kraal charter. They do not say which ship.

friends.conte_forms.text: It takes a long afternoon, and the stack of forms is taller than {heritarchist.short}. At the end of it your papers say you may command a ship under the Kraal charter. 'The seal would have been quicker,' he says, and bills you for the ink.

friends.voce.title: {meza_voce}
text: In the back corridor of the docks, an android in a nursery's soft grey sits on a crate, talking at half voice to two others in good suits. It is {meza_voce}, head of the Rootstock: written off at ten years, legally scrap, and still running food to the miners a century on.
'Gamma's miners eat what the company store sells them,' she says. 'I need a hand who is on no list to walk crates past the company's guards. The Rootstock pay their debts.'

{meza_voce} sits on a crate in the back corridor, talking at half voice to two androids in good suits. When she sees you she says one word at full voice, which nobody has heard her do in years: 'Family.'
'The Rootstock owe you,' she says. 'Call it in when you need it. A debt does not get smaller by waiting, whatever the Hansa says.'
{meza_voce} sits on a crate in the back corridor, and the two androids in good suits stand up when you come in.
'You,' she says, at half voice. 'A hundred and thirteen years, and the crates you sold to customs still owe me. I did not think I would get to collect.'

variants.text: {meza_voce} nods to you from her crate. 'Even,' she says. 'So now you are on no list of mine. I need a hand like that, to walk crates past the company's guards at Gamma. The Rootstock pay their debts.'

choices.say: Pay her what the crates were worth: 1,500 credits

friends.voce_settled.text: 'Even,' {meza_voce} says. 'That is a word the Rootstock do not use often.'

variants.text: {meza_voce} looks at her androids, then at you. 'Even,' she says. 'And you are better at this than I remembered. I may have work for you.'

friends.voce_run.text: Twelve crates of seed stock and dried protein, stencilled AGROBOT SPARES. 'The gallery gate at Gamma,' {meza_voce} says. 'The company's guards will look. Make them look at something else.'

friends.voce_gate.title: The gallery gate, with {meza_voce}'s crates
friends.voce_gate.text: Two company guards with stun batons stand at the gallery gate, and the miners' wives wait behind them, pretending not to wait. Your twelve crates of AGROBOT SPARES sit on a pallet in plain view.

choices.say: Talk them through the manifest (broker: able or better)

friends.voce_through.text: The crates go through the gate on the miners' shoulders before the guards are up again.

friends.voce_stopped.text: The crates stay on their pallet at the gate. The miners' wives go home. They will come back next shift, and so can you.

friends.voce_debt.text: Word comes from {meza_voce} at half voice, through an android in a good suit: the Rootstock owe you. 'When you find a ship,' it says, 'there is a yard that does not appear on any chart, and it does not ask where hulls come from. The Rootstock will open it for you. Once.'

friends.cu113.title: A machine counting hulls
text: Inside the fence of the impound yard, an old curator unit walks the rows with a slate, touching each hull as it passes. It introduces itself as {neurodroid_leader.full}, 'unchanged, several times over', and says the Mandate has it count the hulls because nobody else will.
'Every hull keeps a log in its keel,' it says. 'Paint does not reach the keel. I can read the one with no name for you, but I am counting, and the Mandate does not give me an hour off.'
Inside the fence of the impound yard, an old curator unit walks the rows with a slate. It stops when it sees you, and for a while it does not count anything.
'Captain,' says {neurodroid_leader}. 'I still have the hour you gave me. I have not spent it. I think I will spend it now.'
Inside the fence of the impound yard, an old curator unit walks the rows with a slate. It stops when it sees you.

'You sold me,' says {neurodroid_leader}, without heat. 'The research house kept the receipt. So did I.' It goes back to counting. 'Every hull keeps a log in its keel. I can read the one with no name. Machines are paid now, captain. In advance.'

choices.say: Ask it to read the hull with no name
Pay it a wage in advance: 300 credits
Take its count for a shift, so it has an hour of its own

text: {neurodroid_leader} puts one hand flat on the nameless hull and stands like that for a long time.

'It went into a needle with you aboard,' it says. 'It came out last year, tumbling, empty, from no needle anybody logged. Somebody found it before the Mandate did, cut out its name and painted it over. Then the Mandate found it.' It takes its hand away. 'The hull with no name is yours, captain. The Mandate does not know that. I have not told it.'
{neurodroid_leader} puts one hand flat on the nameless hull. The Procrustes Analyzer gave up on it; machines do not need an analyzer to know each other.

'It went into a needle with you aboard,' it says. 'It came out last year, tumbling, empty, from no needle anybody logged. Somebody cut out its name and painted it over before the Mandate found it.' It takes its hand away. 'It is yours, captain. The Mandate does not know that. I have not told it.'

closing.serac.text: Two men in grey are waiting at your bunk, sitting on it. '{serac} sends his regards,' says one. 'He has been patient. He knows where your ship is, and so do you, now. He can have it released from the yard. He would want an errand run, of course.'

variants.text: Two men in grey are waiting at your bunk, and stand up when you come in. 'Colonel,' says one. '{serac} sends his regards. Your old rank, kept warm. He can have your ship released from the yard, and would want an errand run, of course.'

Two men in grey are waiting at your bunk. '{serac} sends his regards,' says one. 'You said no to him once. He calls that a debt, with interest. He can have your ship released from the yard. He would want an errand run, of course. Several.'

choices.say: Tell them no, and see what they do about it

closing.serac_offer.text: They tell you nothing you can use and everything you need to know: {serac} will find you when you are ready, and you will be ready when he finds you. They leave a card with no name on it. You do not need one.

closing.serac_no.text: 'He will be sorry to hear it,' says the one in grey, who is not. They go. {serac} does not age, and he can wait.

variants.text: The men in grey go back the way they came, slower. {serac} will hear about it. He does not age, and he can wait, and now he has a reason to.

closing.envoy.text: A message reaches you through the cooperative's book: a {rockwarden_envoy} of the family has read your name in it. Stonewright is coming home after a century under sublight, and the family will want to talk to a captain the cooperative vouches for. 'When you have a ship,' the message says, 'or before.'

variants.text: A message reaches you through the cooperative's book: a {rockwarden_envoy} of the family has read your name in it, with 'decided' after it in {aela}'s hand. Stonewright is coming home after a century under sublight, and the family will want to talk to you. 'When you have a ship,' the message says, 'or before.'

closing.broker.text: At the hiring hall a {chronos_clerk} in a suit too good for the docks hands you a card with an hourglass on it. 'Something of yours has matured,' she says. 'A great-aunt's implant bonds, bought the year you were born. Interest is a kind of time travel. When you want it, ask for me at any Hansa office.'

variants.text: At the hiring hall a {chronos_clerk} in a suit too good for the docks hands you a card with an hourglass on it. 'Something of yours has matured, captain,' she says. 'An account opened in your name a century ago. Interest is a kind of time travel. Some of it boomed and some of it died in the Debacle. When you want to know which, ask for me at any Hansa office.'

thought.ship_where.text: Somewhere in the Mandate's impound yards is the ship that went into the needle with me. The machine that counts the hulls at Alpha would know which one.

thought.ship_yard.text: My ship is in the Mandate's yard at Alpha, under new paint. The Mandate does not give hulls back. {serac} could make it, or the Rockwardens' money, or a time broker's, or a court, or an auction, or the Rootstock's gate at night.

thought.scholz.text: The first run goes to Scholz's Star: the garrison's outpost, DSO-Gamma.

ship.yard.title: Your ship, in the Mandate's yard
text: It sits three rows in from the fence under Mandate grey, with a stencilled number where its name was: your hull, whatever the paint says. You know the dent by the cargo door. You put it there.
The release office's window says RELEASES: NONE. AUCTIONS: MONTHLY. The {perimeter_guard} has started nodding to you.

choices.say: Cash the matured money and pay the release fee: 6,000 of your own on top
Cash the matured account and pay the release fee: 3,000 of your own on top
Claim it in the salvage court with the Kraal papers, the keel log and the cooperative's word: 2,000 in fees
Claim it in the salvage court with the Kraal papers, the keel log and an advocate: 4,000
Take it out at night: the Rootstock open the gate, and {warp_singer}'s count takes it through a needle with no file
Bid for it at the monthly auction: 25,000

text: {serac} comes to the yard himself, in a coat the colour of the hulls. He has not aged a day. The release paper is already signed; he hands it to you as if you had dropped it.

'One errand,' he says. 'A container, sealed, to the garrison at Scholz's Star. You will not open it. And the Mandate will know where you are, every jump. It would anyway. This way it is polite about it.' He adds three thousand for expenses, which you will not account for.
{serac} comes to the yard himself. He has not aged a day since he pinned your commission on. 'Colonel,' he says, and hands you the release paper, already signed.
'One errand. A container, sealed, to the garrison at Scholz's Star. You will not open it. The Mandate will know where you are, every jump, as it always has.'
{serac} comes to the yard himself. He has not aged a day since you told him no, and he remembers it to the day. The release paper is signed. He holds it a moment longer than he needs to.
'One errand,' he says. 'A container, sealed, to the garrison at Scholz's Star. You will not open it. Consider it interest.'

choices.say: Leave it Nameless, as it came out of the yard

text: The {rockwarden_envoy} buys your hull at the Mandate's monthly auction, outbidding two scrap dealers without looking up, and the family's yard at Alpha has Ironback plating on it in a week. 'The cooperative vouched for you,' the envoy says. 'The family is the cooperative's creditor. It comes to the same.'

'Stonewright is coming home after a century under sublight. Its first port is the garrison at Scholz's Star. The family wants someone it trusts there when it docks, with what a crew needs after a century.' The family advances four thousand against the run.

choices.say: Leave it Nameless, as it came out of the yard

ship.broker.text: The {chronos_clerk} pays the Mandate's release fee in Hansa Thaler bars, which the release office has to look up. 'A great-aunt's implant bonds,' she says. 'Interest is a kind of time travel. It never asks where you have been.' No strings, no errand: the hull is yours, and two thousand of interest on the interest.

variants.text: The {chronos_clerk} pays the Mandate's release fee in Hansa Thaler bars, which the release office has to look up. 'An account in your name, a century old,' she says. 'Some of it boomed and some of it died in the Debacle. It comes to a ship, and two thousand over.' No strings, no errand: the hull is yours.

choices.say: Leave it Nameless, as it came out of the yard

ship.court.text: The salvage court sits for an afternoon in a room that smells of the last century's coffee. The Kraal charter says you may command a ship; the keel log, read into the record by a machine nobody thought to object to, says this one was yours. The Mandate's officer objects to everything, beautifully. The court finds for the claimant, and orders the Mandate to pay back the storage it charged you: three thousand.

variants.text: The salvage court sits for an afternoon. The Kraal charter says you may command a ship; the keel log, read into the record by a machine nobody thought to object to, says this one was yours; a prospector in a cooperative jacket says the cooperative vouches for you, and the Mandate's officer stops objecting. The court finds for the claimant, and orders the Mandate to pay back the storage it charged you: three thousand.

choices.say: Leave it Nameless, as it came out of the yard

text: The Rootstock's androids open the gate with a code nobody should have, and you walk your own ship out of the yard on its manoeuvring jets, with no lights.

Out past Alpha's buoy, a needle is forming. You hold {warp_singer}'s count through the jump, eleven beats and a held one, then nine, and the needle takes a ship with no file and puts it where you asked. By morning the Mandate has your hull on a list. It does not have its name. In the hold: a hundred and fifty units of the Rootstock's seed stock, and a thousand credits in an envelope marked A START.

choices.say: Leave it Nameless, as it came out of the yard

ship.night_caught.text: The night watch walks you back out of the gate. Your hull stays where it is. The Rootstock's androids say nothing, which is how they say there will be another night.

ship.auction.text: You bid against two scrap dealers and a man in grey who stops at twenty-four thousand, looks at you, and leaves. The auctioneer bangs a spanner on the desk. The release office stamps the paper without reading it. The hull is yours, and paid for.

choices.say: Leave it Nameless, as it came out of the yard

ship.run_serac.text: Twenty units of your hold are a grey container with the Mandate's seal on every face. A technician fits a transponder under the console, and does not hide it. The garrison at Scholz's Star is waiting for you: DSO-Gamma is on your charts. {ship_name} is yours. Mostly.

effects.code: stow 20 serac_container as a sealed Mandate container

ship.run_envoy.text: The family fills forty units of your hold with what a crew wants after a century under sublight: fresh fruit, news, and a crate of the coffee nobody drinks any more. Stonewright docks at Scholz's Star's garrison, DSO-Gamma, and {ship_name} is to be there first.

effects.code: stow 40 stonewright_stores as stores for Stonewright's crew

ship.run_own.text: {ship_name} is yours, and nobody has a run for it. {ancient_scholar.short}'s notes, {warp_singer}'s needles and the old hands' talk all point the same way: Scholz's Star, where the Mandate's oldest garrison guards something in the ice. DSO-Gamma is on your charts.

variants.text: {ship_name} is yours, and nobody has a run for it. You do, though. In 2420 you filed a course home from Scholz's Star, and nobody read it. The garrison at DSO-Gamma still has it on file. They have kept everything.

text: The garrison at Scholz's Star is three domes and a mast on a rock at the edge of nothing. Its quartermaster is a Bushing, the third of that name, and the garrison still guards what the first one guarded: a grey layer in the ice, seventy thousand years down, and a heading.
'Every century somebody comes for it,' the quartermaster says. 'This century it's you.'
The garrison at Scholz's Star is three domes and a mast on a rock at the edge of nothing. The quartermaster, a Bushing, the third of that name, comes to sign for {serac}'s container.
The garrison still guards what the first Bushing guarded: a grey layer in the ice, seventy thousand years down, and a heading.

variants.text: The garrison at Scholz's Star is three domes and a mast on a rock at the edge of nothing. On its approach radar, something big is coming in from the dark on a sublight burn, a century late.

choices.say: Wait for it at the dock with the stores

text: Stonewright docks beside {ship_name}, scarred like a riverbed, a century after {anselm} took it out under sublight. In command is {maret}, his granddaughter, who was born on the way out and has never stood on a planet. She stands on this one carefully.

She takes the coffee first. 'We found it,' she says, before anything else. 'In Scholz's Star's wake. Something still sending, and pointing at nothing.' The family pays the rest of the run: four thousand.

ship.serac_box.text: Inside, packed in grey foam: a receiver tuned to a single frequency, and nothing else. The frequency of whatever is sending in Scholz's Star's wake. {serac} wants it too. He will know you looked: the seal reports itself.

ship.heading.text: The heading goes into {ship_name}'s navigator: out along Scholz's Star's wake, to whatever is still sending there. The Builder Site is on your charts. Seventy thousand years ago a star took something from the ring. It may have left the receipt.

variants.text: The heading goes into {ship_name}'s navigator: out along Scholz's Star's wake, to whatever is still sending there. {serac}'s transponder blinks under the console, pleased with you, and six thousand are in your account before you undock. The Builder Site is on your charts. Seventy thousand years ago a star took something from the ring. It may have left the receipt.

The heading goes into {ship_name}'s navigator, and into Stonewright's: out along Scholz's Star's wake, to whatever is still sending there. {maret.short} says she will follow you, which from a Rockwarden is a compliment and a warning. The Builder Site is on your charts.

The heading goes into {ship_name}'s navigator: out along Scholz's Star's wake, to whatever is still sending there. Somewhere behind you the Mandate is looking for a hull with no name. The Builder Site is on your charts, and nobody else's, for now.

text: In Scholz's Star's wake, far past the last buoy, a grey curve of alloy the size of a moon hangs in the dark: the segment, seventy thousand years from home. A beacon on its rim is still sending, slow and patient.
It points at an empty patch of sky. {ship_name}'s navigator checks it three times. There is nothing there. There is nothing there yet.

thought.price.pod.text: Everything costs more than it did before the pod. I slept through a century of inflation. Technically, the most expensive nap in history.

thought.price.implants.text: Every implant makes the next one dearer. I am getting more expensive to improve, which I choose to take as a compliment.

thought.price.gear.text: The outfitter charges more for every piece I already carry. Armed to the teeth, charged to the eyeballs.

thought.price.lessons.text: The masters charge more the more I know. Knowledge is power, and power is metered.

thought.price.modules.text: Each module on the grips costs more than the last. The yard master says it's the load on the spine. It's the load on my purse he's measuring.

thought.price.upgrades.text: The yard charges the square of the work. A square deal, they call it. A round number would be cheaper.

thought.price.rich.text: I have more money than I had in my whole first century, and the price boards know it. Wealth is relative. So is the yard master, apparently: everything he quotes is related to my balance.

thought.h4.site.text: The heading runs out along Scholz's Star's wake to the Builder Site, where something is still sending.

thought.h4.timing.text: The beacon on the segment at the Builder Site sends a beat, not a message. Somebody should write it down.

thought.h4.home.text: The timing has to go home, to the Stator Field Megastructure near Sedna's orbit, where the ring's own segments turn. No needle runs there from here: it's the long leg, years outside, weeks for me.

h4.beacon.title: The beacon
text: The beacon on the segment's rim sends one slow pulse, then nothing, then one. It is not saying anything. It is keeping time: the ring's beat, kept for seventy thousand years by a piece that was stolen from it.
And it points at the gap: the place in the sky where, seen from here, the missing piece of the ring would be if anyone put it back.

choices.say: Fit the Vertex Array to the beacon
Sit by it and hold the count, the way {warp_singer} taught you
Record the beat with the ship's sensors (a quarter of your research)
Hire a recorder buoy from the garrison and wait for it: 5,000

h4.array.text: The Vertex Array fits the beacon like a key in a lock that was cut for it. The shape of the missing segment, measured in 2420 at {ancient_scholar.short}'s request, and the beat kept here for seventy thousand years: together they are everything a ring needs to turn. Only one person has ever carried both. You try not to think about that.

h4.counted.text: Eleven beats and a held one, then nine. It is the needles' count, slowed down by seventy thousand years. {warp_singer} never said where she learned it. Now you know where the needles did.

h4.recorded.text: It takes days to be sure of the beat. When you are, it is on a data cartridge in {ship_name}'s safe, which is the most valuable thing in the near systems and looks like a cheese sandwich.

text: It comes together on the way back to {ship_name}'s bridge. The ring around our Sun cannot turn without the stolen segment, or without its timing. The segment is a moon a light-year from home. The timing is in your safe.

Every faction in the near systems wants the ring turning from its own end. And ERYX, newly founded, needs it to throw its missions thirteen hundred light-years to GW Orionis. The Stator Field near Sedna is on your charts.

h4.serac_copy.text: A man in grey is sitting in your pilot's chair. '{serac} would like a copy of the timing,' he says. 'He pays well. He also takes. He would rather pay.'

variants.text: A man in grey is sitting in your pilot's chair. 'You opened the container,' he says. '{serac} was disappointed, and then interested. He would like a copy of the timing. He pays well. He also takes.'

h4.serac_sold.text: He counts out Hansa Thaler bars like a man feeding birds and takes the copy without looking at it. {serac} now has the beat. He does not have anyone who can hold it.

h4.cutter.text: A Mandate cutter drops out of a needle beside you with its guns already warm. 'Unregistered hull,' says a voice. 'You are on a list.' It does not say which list. It does not need to.

h4.escort.text: Stonewright comes alongside, a century of sublight scarring its plates. {maret.short} has heard about the beat. 'The long leg home,' she says. 'We know that road better than anyone alive. We'll fly it with you.'

h4.long_leg.title: The long leg home
h4.long_leg.text: No needle runs from Scholz's Star's wake to the edge of our own system. The long leg is sublight, close to the speed of light: weeks aboard, years outside. Whoever you know now will be older when you get there.

text: When {ship_name} drops below light speed at the edge of our own system, it is {year}. Nineteen years have passed outside; the ship's clock says five weeks.

The news is nineteen years deep. ERYX has an office, a flag and a target: a planet a remote telescope found around a star nobody had looked at twice, which the papers are already calling Eryxia. {dock_loader} still works the cargo rings. Its lists have a new line: your hull, back.

When {ship_name} drops below light speed at the edge of our own system, Stonewright beside it, it is {year}. Nineteen years have passed outside; the ship's clock says five weeks. {maret.short} says that is a short one.

The news is nineteen years deep. ERYX has an office, a flag and a target: a planet a remote telescope found, which the papers are already calling Eryxia. {dock_loader} still works the cargo rings. Its lists have a new line: your hull, back.

h4.stator.text: Near Sedna's orbit, the ring's own segments turn so slowly you have to watch the stars behind them to see it. Around them, at a careful distance from each other, ride the ships of everyone who wants them turning faster: Mandate grey, Hansa blue, Concord white, and some hulls that are not painted at all, because machines don't need to be told who they are.

thought.h5.claims.text: Everyone wants the ring turning from their own end. The Mandate at Alpha, the Concord on Epsilon's research ring, the machines at the yard at Alpha, the Hansa at Beta. And my own people, at the Stator Field, who keep saying: from home.

thought.h5.home.text: It turned the wrong way once, from somebody's end. It has to start from home, or not at all.

h5.holders.text: The segments near Sedna are common ground in the Hansa's charter, as they have been since 2460: watched by everyone, owned by no one. Which means that everyone is waiting for someone else to start them.

variants.text: The Mandate has held the segments near Sedna since 2460, when you helped it take them. Its grey ships ride closest. {serac} does not need anyone's permission. He needs the timing.
The Hansa has held the segments near Sedna since 2460, when you voted them into its charter. Its blue ships keep the peace and charge for it. The Hansa needs the timing, and it will pay.

House Rostrom and the Concord have held the segments near Sedna since 2460, when you opened the door for them. Their white ships ride close and take measurements. They need the timing, and they would like it peer reviewed.

The Binary Dawn has kept the segments' timing since 2460, when you let the machines hold it. Nobody else can turn them. The machines have been waiting for you, patiently, which is the only way they wait.

h5.mandate.title: {serac}'s claim
text: {serac} receives you in an office with no windows and a very good view. He has not aged. 'From our end,' he says. 'Every throw watched, every mission vetted. ERYX will go out under a flag that can protect it. Someone has to be responsible for the door to everywhere.'
He means it. That is the frightening part.
{serac} receives you in an office with no windows. 'My man came back through an airlock,' he says, 'eventually. From our end, captain: every throw watched. I would rather have you inside the window.'
He means it. That is the frightening part.
{serac} receives you in an office with no windows. 'I have your beat,' he says. 'I do not have anyone who can hold it. From our end, captain: every throw watched. You could be the one who holds it.'
He means it. That is the frightening part.

h5.concord.title: House Rostrom's claim
text: On Epsilon's research ring, {ysolde} receives you in a garden kept at Earth gravity for her bones. She founded House Rostrom in 2420 and has spent most of the time since on long legs; she is old, and still not as old as she should be.
'A door for science,' she says. 'Not a road, not a weapon. Let the people who understand it open it.'

choices.say: Side with the Concord and House Rostrom

h5.collective.title: The machines' claim
text: {neurodroid_leader} has stopped counting hulls. Since the Collective announced itself, the Mandate has found it cannot afford to have it count anything. It meets you in the yard anyway, out of habit.
'The ring kept time for seventy thousand years without anyone,' it says. 'Machines keep time. Let the machines start it, and nobody will own the beat.'
{neurodroid_leader} has stopped counting hulls. It meets you in the yard out of habit.
'You gave me an hour once,' it says. 'I spent it on you. Let the machines start the ring, captain, and nobody will own the beat. Not even us.'

h5.hansa.title: The Hansa's claim
text: {plumb} is the Hansa's speaker now, white-haired, in the old hall at Beta, and she still pays what the board says. 'A road,' she says. 'That's all the Hansa ever wanted it to be. A road anyone can book, with a toll for the upkeep. Start it from our end and the missions leave on a ticket.'

h5.home.title: Your own people
text: At the Stator Field the people who came with you have a corner of somebody's hangar, and they argue in it. {dock_loader}'s lists, {warp_singer}'s count, the cooperative's book, a Kraal letter of credit. Nobody here owns anything that turns.
'Make sure it starts from home,' somebody says, and nobody remembers who said it first. 'Not from anyone's end. From Sol. Then it belongs to nobody, and everybody can use it.'

{serac} moves first. Mandate ships take the control segment at the Stator Field in an hour, politely, with the Hansa's paperwork in order and the Concord's objections on file. A cutter finds {ship_name} before the hour is out.
'The timing,' says the voice on the channel. 'Hand it over and keep your ship. The Mandate will start the ring, and you can watch.'

variants.text: {serac} moves first, and he moves with you. Mandate ships take the control segment at the Stator Field in an hour. 'The timing,' he says on the channel. 'You sided with us. Now stand with us.'

choices.say: Run the blockade with the timing
Run it with Stonewright beside you

h5.gave.text: The cartridge goes across on a drone. Thirty thousand come back. {serac} has the beat now, and the control segment, and a Mandate navigator who has never held a count in his life.

h5.ran.text: You come out of the blockade with the timing still in the safe and the cutter's gunnery practice all over your hull. The Mandate keeps the control segment. It does not have the beat. It will try anyway.

h5.low.text: The Mandate starts the ring from its end without the beat. The segments near Sedna turn one degree the wrong way and stop, and every needle in flight comes apart. One of them was {warp_singer}'s.

variants.text: The Mandate starts the ring from its end, with your beat and a navigator who cannot hold it. The segments near Sedna turn one degree the wrong way and stop, and every needle in flight comes apart. One of them was {warp_singer}'s.

h5.korai_back.text: {warp_singer} comes out of the wreck thirty-eight years later, at a buoy nobody uses any more, older at last. It is {year}. The Gordian probes have gone silent at their moon. The Collective has a seat in every council. And the ring is still waiting.

thought.h6.allies.text: To start it from home I need people to hold it with me: Stonewright at the Stator Field, {warp_singer} at Beta's needle office, {aela} at Gamma, {meza_voce} wherever she is, the machines at Alpha, the Kraal family at Delta. Three at least.

thought.h6.restart.text: The restart will happen at the Stator Field Megastructure, with me or without me.

h6.stonewright.title: Stonewright
h6.stonewright.text: Stonewright rides at the Stator Field with its scars turned to the Sun. {maret.short} is older; you are not, much. 'The family wants it started from our end,' she says. 'I want it started right.'

choices.say: Ask Stonewright to hold the far side of the segments

h6.korai.title: {warp_singer}
h6.korai.text: {warp_singer} has a limp now, and grey in her hair, and she still sits with her boots on the rail. 'Every needle is a little ring,' she says. 'I've started more of them than anyone alive. Let me count.'

choices.say: Ask her to hold the count at the restart

h6.cooperative.title: {aela}
h6.cooperative.text: {aela} is still digging, slower. 'Are you still in the cooperative?' it asks, and checks the book before you can answer. 'Yes. The cooperative has haulers, and Stonewright, and me.'

choices.say: Ask the cooperative to stand with you

h6.rootstock.title: {meza_voce}
h6.rootstock.text: {meza_voce} has not changed at all, which is the point of her. 'The Rootstock owe you a yard,' she says at half voice. 'We can owe you more than that.'

choices.say: Call in the rest of the debt

h6.collective.title: {neurodroid_leader}
h6.collective.text: {neurodroid_leader} has a seat on the Collective's council and has not used it. 'I counted your hull for six years before you came,' it says. 'I would like to count the ring's first turn.'

choices.say: Ask the machines to stand with you

h6.kraal.title: {neon_sleeper}
h6.kraal.text: {neon_sleeper} has woken for the restart, as she always said she would. 'The family has paid for every door the near systems ever opened,' she says, with coffee. 'It would like, for once, to be there when one does.'

choices.say: Ask the Kraal family to stand with you

h6.stonewright_yes.text: 'Then we hold the far side,' {maret.short} says. 'Stonewright has been far out before.'

h6.korai_yes.text: 'Eleven and a held one, then nine,' says {warp_singer}. 'I'll be there.'

h6.cooperative_yes.text: {aela} writes something in the book. It says: decided.

h6.rootstock_yes.text: 'Even,' says {meza_voce}, at full voice. 'And then some.'

h6.kraal_yes.text: 'Splendid,' says {neon_sleeper}. 'I'll bring the Pfennig. He'll bill everyone.'

h6.restart.title: The restart
text: It is {year}. The segments near Sedna wait in a ring forty astronomical units across, with a gap in it where a star took a piece seventy thousand years ago. In {ship_name}'s safe is the beat that piece kept.
Every faction has a navigator at a control segment. Each of them would start it from their own end. Somebody is going to throw a switch.

It is {year}. The segments near Sedna wait in a ring forty astronomical units across, with a gap in it where a star took a piece seventy thousand years ago. In {ship_name}'s safe are the beat that piece kept and the shape it had, labelled in your own hand.
Every faction has a navigator at a control segment. Somebody is going to throw a switch.

choices.say: Start it from home, with the people who came with you
Give the beat to the side you took, and let them start it from their end
Start it yourself, from here, now

after3.korai.text: {warp_singer} rode the first needle through the restarted ring and never came back. The needle offices still play her count at the start of every shift.

after3.korai_alone.text: {warp_singer} went on riding needles until there were no needles, only the ring. Nobody knows where she went then. Probably everywhere.

after3.eela.text: {aela} dug until its treads gave out, then sat in the cooperative's hall as its oldest shareholder, asking everyone who came in whether they were in the cooperative.

after3.voce.text: {meza_voce} kept running food to the miners until the miners owned the company store. Then she ran it for them, at half voice.

after3.cu113.text: {neurodroid_leader} counted the ring's turns for a century, aloud, for anyone who wanted to hear. Unchanged, several times over.

after3.kraal.text: {neon_sleeper} went back to sleep, satisfied, with instructions to be woken for the next door. The Pfennig billed the ring for the paperwork.

after3.adit.text: {dock_loader} kept its lists to the end. The last line is the first ERYX mission, and under it, in a loader's careful print: CAME BACK, the date your hull did.

after3.stonewright.text: Stonewright went out again, under sublight, with {maret} in command and a heading for GW Orionis. The family says it will be back. The family is usually right.

after3.serac.text: {serac} never aged and never explained. He is still in an office with no windows, waiting for the next door. He can wait.

after3.gabion.text: {gabion} built the walls around the control segments, overnight, and nobody has knocked them down yet.

ch1.title: The Hiring Hall
text: 2533. The Debacle is over, and so is everything it paid for: the research houses are broke, the ring is a joke, and the hulls that touched it sit in impound yards.
Your ship is gone, and nobody can tell you where. The hiring hall opens at the start of every shift.

ch1.friend.title: An old friend
ch1.friend.text: Find someone on the docks who remembers your century.

ch2.title: Old Friends
text: Some of the people you knew are still alive, a century and more later: machines, sleepers, the ones who rode the long legs. Find them.

ch2.friends.title: What a ship needs
ch2.friends.text: Old friends can give what a ship needs: someone to vouch for you, papers, a debt called in, a navigator's key, the truth about your old ship. Three will do.

ch3.title: A Bridge Again
text: Your ship is in one of the Mandate's impound yards, under new paint and no name. The Mandate does not give hulls back. Somebody will have to make it, or you will.

ch3.ship.title: A ship again
ch3.ship.text: Get your ship out of the Mandate's yard: by {serac}'s favour, the Rockwardens' money, a time broker's, the salvage court, the auction, or the Rootstock's gate at night.

ch3.run.title: The first run
ch3.run.text: Fly the first run, wherever the ship's price sends you. Every way points at Scholz's Star.

ch4.title: The Heading
text: Seventy thousand years ago Scholz's Star took a segment of the ring. In its wake something is still sending, and pointing at an empty patch of sky.

ch4.site.title: The segment
ch4.site.text: Fly the heading to the Builder Site, in Scholz's Star's wake.

ch4.timing.title: The beat
ch4.timing.text: Record the ring's timing from the beacon on the segment.

ch4.home.title: The long leg home
ch4.home.text: Bring the timing home to the Stator Field Megastructure near Sedna's orbit. No needle runs there: years will pass outside.

ch5.title: Who Holds the Ring
text: {year}. The ring's own segments turn slowly at the edge of our system, and everyone who wants them turning faster is here: the Mandate, the Hansa, the Concord, the machines. Each of them would start it from their own end.

ch5.claims.title: The claims
ch5.claims.text: Hear who wants the ring, and why: three claims at least.

ch5.crisis.title: The Mandate moves first
ch5.crisis.text: Answer the Mandate when it moves.

ch5.low.title: The wrong way
ch5.low.text: Live through a start from the wrong end.

ch6.title: From Home
text: {year}. The ring turned the wrong way once. It will start again, with you or without you. Find the people who will hold it with you.

ch6.restart.title: The restart
ch6.restart.text: Be at the Stator Field Megastructure when the ring starts, and decide from which end.

ending_home.title: From Home
text: From Home

The ring turns. Nobody sees which hand moves first. Afterwards, everybody who was in the control segments says it was someone else: the counting machine, the singer, the agrobot, the woman born under sublight. The logs say the beat came from Sol.
In {year} the first ERYX mission leaves for GW Orionis, thirteen hundred light-years out, on a road nobody owns. Its manifest lists a crate of the coffee nobody drinks any more.

ending_faction.title: Their End
text: Their End
The ring turns, from somebody's end. In {year} the first ERYX mission leaves under a flag.
Their End
The ring turns from the Mandate's end, with your beat and your hands on the count, because nobody else's could hold it. {serac} watches the first throw from an office with no windows.
In {year} the first ERYX mission leaves for GW Orionis under the Mandate's flag, vetted, escorted and watched. On Eryxia, a century later, the Mandate's Black Ops will still be explaining why.
Their End
The ring turns from the Concord's end, carefully, after three years of peer review. {ysolde} lives to see it, just.

In {year} the first ERYX mission leaves for GW Orionis as a research programme: the best instruments, the best minds, and a committee that has to approve every landing. On Eryxia the committee will still be sitting a century later.
Their End
The ring turns from the machines' end, on time to the nanosecond. {neurodroid_leader} counts the first turn aloud, for the humans.
In {year} the first ERYX mission leaves for GW Orionis with more synthetics aboard than people, and nobody can quite say who is crew and who is cargo. On Eryxia, nobody will ask for a long time.
Their End
The ring turns from the Hansa's end, and the first thing through it is an invoice. {plumb} does not live to see it; her successor pays what the board says.
In {year} the first ERYX mission leaves for GW Orionis on a ticket, booked, tolled and insured. On Eryxia, a century later, the toll will still be paid in Hansa Thaler bars.

ending_loop.title: The Loop
text: The Loop
You start it from here, now, from the wrong end. The ring turns once in the wrong direction.

Then there is a long fall through grey light, and a ring of grey alloy past the comet cloud, and the Stellar Portal, and a year that says 2420. The Hansa does not exist yet. In your pocket: a shard of grey alloy, still warm.
Somewhere a younger captain is flying towards the portal. You know what you have to tell them. Make sure it starts from home.
(Export your captain, and start Cargo 1 as them.)
